title: Confirming and Refuting Research Hypotheses About the Trampling of Alpine Vegetation (a Study from the Belianske Tatras, Slovakia)
content: Although the topic of trampling of alpine vegetation has been addressed by many authors in recent years, there are still many unanswered questions. Areas unsuitable for enormous numbers of tourists are particularly problematic. Such an area is the limestone Belianske Tatras, closed to tourists since 1978, with the exception of a trail that has been accessible in one direction since 1993 and in both directions since 2008 as an educational trail. Since there is renewed discussion about making the Belianske Tatras accessible to tourists, we sought answers to the hypotheses: (1.) whether regenerated communities are more resistant to trampling than the native ones, (2.) whether all individual species in different communities react to trampling in the same way, and (3.) whether some species can become extinct after being trampled. We conducted the research in the form of experimental research in three communities – in 2008 in the native ones and in 2022 in the regenerated ones, with a modification of the methodology from the study by Cole and Bayfield (1993). Regenerated communities respond as more resistant, but at the expense of the extinction of some species in the form of a delayed response. Individual species respond differently in different communities.
